agent_trace.summary: On abdominal CT, the small bowel is normally seen as centrally located bowel loops, often above the rectum and sometimes around the bladder depending on the slice level and bladder distention. For an abnormality-description question, attention should focus on bowel caliber, wall thickening, abnormal location, and any associated retroperitoneal or abdominal wall soft-tissue changes.

key_facts: Small bowel loops are a normal visible structure on abdominal CT.
Their expected position is generally within the central abdomen, often above the rectum.
Abnormal bowel findings on CT may include dilation, obstruction, wall thickening, or displacement.
Retroperitoneal soft tissues and the abdominal wall can show edema, inflammation, or mass effect when disease is present.
